summary: Root cause proven from both bundles + Angular 16 runtime: Ivy fires input setters in template order (splitPos before splitTopEl) whereas Angular 8 View Engine applied them in directive-declaration order (splitTopEl[0] before splitPos[5]); set splitPos dereferences the not-yet-populated this.splitTopEl -> classList error. App-latent assumption (b) exposed by genuine Ivy ordering change (a); template and component are byte-identical to source (not c). But Angular 16 ships NO vendor mechanism/provider/config to restore VE input ordering, so the packet's prescribed fix shape (vendor-guarded, app-source-unchanged) is unrealizable; the only working generic fix reorders authored template bindings, violating 'App source stays as its authors wrote it'. Made no file changes.
open_questions: No Angular provider/config/compiler-flag exists to reorder Ivy input-setter invocation (verified in core.mjs 16.2.12). Which constraint should be relaxed? Option A: permit a generic, analyzer-proven, semantics-preserving TEMPLATE-BINDING-REORDER capability (moves [splitTopEl] before [splitPos] at proven call sites) — fixes the lane but edits authored template attribute order (relaxes 'App source stays as its authors wrote it'). Option B: permit a minimal app-source null-guard on the setter (relaxes the no-app-logic-patch rule). Option C: accept the regression as a declared framework-behavior difference (like the two style deltas) with no code fix.

Confirm the intended fix was believed to have a vendor mechanism: if the packet author assumed an Angular provider analogous to callSetDisabledState exists for input ordering, that assumption is false — please re-scope to one of the options above.

If Option A is chosen: confirm reordering authored template attributes is acceptable as migration output (precedent split-element-successor only retags removed elements; forms-legacy only adds a provider — neither reorders authored attributes), and confirm the rebuild x2 + behavior-check scope stays as specified.
